newsitem.title: UK: SW Water to raise interim div 20.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: SW Water to raise interim div 20.4 pct.

text.p: South West Water Plc said it will raise it interim dividend by 20.4 percent to 11.8 pence per share when it announces its results on November 14.
The company also announced it will pay a 15 stg rebate to customers in June 1997.
Earlier, the UK Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) announced its decision not to permit proposed bids by Wessex and Severn Trent Plc for South West Water.
Trade Secretary Ian Lang supported the recommendations of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, which had said the takeovers would be against the public interest.
South West said it would continue its strategy of emhancing the value of its service to customers and of maximising the benefits of its capital programme.
South West's chairman Keith Court said the DTI decsion had ended a period of uncertainty.

"Despite the distraction caused by the proposed bids, we have made major strides in increasing the efficiency of our core water business and carefully growing our non-regulated businesses," Court said in a statement.
At 1120 GMT, South West Water shares were 128 pence lower at 577.5 haveing earlier touched a low of 565 pence per share. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
